rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: The wording that God rewards the charitable is an indirect expression that avoids a lie, since the brothers regarded Joseph as an unbelieving king; the same explanation is attributed to al-Dahhak.
rows.anchor: قال النقاش : وفي العدول عن إن الله تعالى يجزيك بصدقتك إلى ما في النظم الكريم مندوحة عن الكذب فهو من المعاريض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They led with hardship to awaken Joseph's pity and compassion, hoping to use that mercy to secure their father's aim.
rows.anchor: فيما سلكوه استجلابا للشفقة والرحمة فكأنهم أرادوا أن يملأوا حياض قلبه من نميرها

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Their request to be dealt with charitably can carry either interpretation, and Joseph may have understood it as a request to return Benjamin.
rows.anchor: قولهم ( وتصدق ) الخ كلام ذو وجهين فانه يحتمل الحمل على المحملين فلعله عليه السلام حمله على طلب الرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph mentions the harm done to both himself and his brother because both were subjected to their brothers' exclusion and humiliation, leaving Joseph unable to speak except in weakness.
rows.anchor: تعرض لما فعل به أيضا لاشتراكهما في وقوع الفعل عليهما فان المراد بذلك افرادهم له عنه وإذلاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether they now recognize the ugliness of what they did in their ignorance and whether that ignorance has passed.
rows.anchor: ما فعلتموه زمان جهلكم قبحه وزال ذلك الجهل أم لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi reads the question as gentle admonition and counsel to stop, not revenge: Joseph relinquishes personal satisfaction while subtly reproaching their culpable ignorance and appealing to both divine and fraternal rights.
rows.anchor: والظاهر لهذا أن ذلك لم يكن تشفيا بل حث على الاقلاع ونصح لهم لما رأى من عجزهم وتمسكنهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: The speech may be detached from the brothers' words and redirect them from other requests to their duty to seek Benjamin; Joseph may have learned their father's instruction by revelation or inspiration.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون هذا الكلام منه عليه السلام منقطعا عن كلامهم وتنبيها لهم عما حقهم ووظيفتهم

rows.speaker: ابن إسحق
rows.claim: When the brothers pleaded, Joseph relented, cried uncontrollably, and began identifying himself; he meant by their deeds his mistreatment and exclusion of Joseph and their cruelty to Benjamin.
rows.anchor: روى عن ابن إسحق أنهم لما استعطفوه رق لهم ورحمهم حتى أنه ارفض دمعه باكيا ولم يملك نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph did not mention how they hurt their father, out of respect for Jacob; that wrong was already included as a consequence of what he had named.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر لهم ما آذوا به أباهم على ماقيل تعظيما لقدره وتفخيما لشأنه أن يذكره مع نفسه وأخيه

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: A letter from Jacob recounts the family's trials: Abraham survived the fire, Isaac the knife, Jacob lost his sight grieving Joseph, and the brothers later accused Benjamin of theft; Jacob says his family does not steal and threatens a curse if Benjamin is not returned.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنهم أدوا اليه كتابا من أبيهم وصورته كما في الكشاف من يعقوب اسرائيل الله بن إسحاق ذبيح الله

rows.speaker: أبو روق
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits from Abu Rوق a report similar to the account of Jacob's letter pleading for Benjamin's return.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن أبي روق نحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After reading the letter, Joseph could not contain himself; a report says he wept and replied that patience like theirs would bring success.
rows.anchor: فلما قرأ يوسف عليه السلام الكتاب لم يتمالك وعيل صبره فقال لهم ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred reading is that the brothers were genuinely ignorant of the evil of their act; another view calls them ignorant because they acted against what they knew.
rows.anchor: هذا وما أشرنا اليه من كون المراد إثبات الجهل لهم حقيقة هو الظاهر وقيل : لم يرد نفي العلم عنهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: They are said to have been ignorant because they were still children before reaching maturity, but Alusi rejects this as inconsistent with the account that they were a strong band and with the facts of the story.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس والحسن ( جاهلون ) صبيان قبل أن تبلغوا أو أن الحلم والرزانة وتعقب بأنه ليس بالوجه

rows.speaker: التحرير
rows.claim: Al-Tahrir takes the question as rhetorical confirmation and rebuke, meaning how grave their offense was, as in asking whether someone knows whom they disobeyed; Alusi says this is not the sound interpretation.
rows.anchor: وزعم في التحرير أن قول الجمهور : إن الاستفهام للتقرير والتوبيخ ومراده عليه السلام تعظيم الواقعة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another reading takes هل as قد, as in the cited verse, while retaining the purpose of rebuke; Alusi rejects this and the preceding account in favor of his earlier explanation.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هل بمعنى قد كما في ( هل أتى على الانسان حين من الدهر ) والمقصود هو التوبيخ أيضا

rows.speaker: الثعلبي
rows.claim: Al-Tha'labi tells an account in which Joseph angrily ordered his brothers killed, then relented when they wept; Alusi says this story is utterly unsound.
rows.anchor: ومن الغريب الذي لايصح البتة ما حكاه الثعلبي أنه عليه السلام حين قالوا له ماقالوا غضب عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi prefers that God's favor meant the brothers were surpassed through piety and patience; other reports explain it by kingship, patience and knowledge, forbearance, or a wider list of virtues and royal power.
rows.anchor: أي اختارك وفضلك علينا بالتقوى والصبر وقيل : بالملك وقيل : بالصبر والعلم ورويا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: سليمان الدمشقي
rows.claim: Sulayman al-Dimashqi explains God's favor as Joseph's forbearance and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وقيل : بالحلم والصفح ذكره سليمان الدمشقي

rows.speaker: صاحب الغنيان
rows.claim: The author of al-Ghunyān lists Joseph's good character and appearance, knowledge, forbearance, beneficence, kingship, patience with their harm, and power as reasons for God's favor.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب الغنيان : بحسن الخلق والخلق والعلم والحلم والاحسان والملك والسلطان والصبر على أذانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers admit they were deliberate sinners; the circumstantial conjunction marks their state, إِنّ is lightened with an implicit pronoun of شأن, and the lām in the predicate is the shifted emphatic lām.
rows.anchor: أي لمتعمدين للذنب إذ فعلنا ما فعلنا ولذلك أعزك وأذلنا فالواو حالية و ( إن ) مخففة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling themselves intentional sinners both seeks Joseph's kindness and confesses their wrongdoing with an implicit signal of repentance.
rows.anchor: من الاستنزال لاحسانه عليه السلام والاعتراف بما صدر منهم في حقه مع الاشعار بالتوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خاطئين derives from a verb for intentional sin, unlike أخطأ, which describes aiming at what is right but failing to attain it.
rows.anchor: من خطيء إذا تعمد وأما اخطأ فقصد الصواب ولم يوفق له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تثريب means blame or reproach; its root is the thin fat on the inner body, and the form denotes removal, metaphorically likening blame that exposes faults to stripping away what gives the face its fullness and beauty.
rows.anchor: وأصله من الثرب وهو الشحم الرقيق في الجوف وعلى الكرش وصيغة التفعيل للسلب أي ازالة الثرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison joins the loss of fat and the loss of reputation: both bring deficiency after completeness and remove what gives beauty.
rows.anchor: فالجامع بينهما طريان النقص بعد الكمال وازالة ما به الكمال والجمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun after لا is تثريب; عليكم is linked to an omitted predicate, and اليوم can modify that predicate or its adverbial phrase. Limiting the assurance to today does not imply reproach later, since Joseph's restraint at their first meeting makes later reproach still less likely.
rows.anchor: وليس التقييد به لافادة وقوع التثريب في غيره فانه عليه السلام اذا لم يثرب أول لقائه واشتعال ناره فبعده بطريق الاولى

rows.speaker: المرتضى
rows.claim: Al-Murtada reads اليوم as standing for all time, like the cited poetic lines about today's reversal of fortune.
rows.anchor: وقال المرتضى : إن ( اليوم ) موضوع موضع الزمان كله كقوله : اليوم يرحمنا من كان يغبطنا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows اليوم to attach to تثريب; Abu Hayyan objects that عليكم intervenes between the verbal noun and its complement, and that this analysis would make the noun quasi-annexed and therefore declinable with tanwin.
rows.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري تعلقه بتثريب وتعقبه أبو حيان قائلا : لايجوز ذلك لأن التثريب مصدر

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa also rejects attaching اليوم to تثريب, arguing that the resulting quasi-annexed noun would have to be declinable and take tanwin.
rows.anchor: وكذا منع ذلك أبو البقاء وعالمه بلزوم الاعراب والتنوين أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection based on tanwin is not universal: grammatical texts and the agreed wording of a hadith show quasi-annexed nouns without tanwin, though grammarians disagree whether such forms are built or merely unmarked for tanwin.
rows.anchor: واعترض بأن المصرح به في متون النحو بأن شبيه المضاف سمع فيه عدم التنوين نحو لا طالع جبلا

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Al-Radi says an adverb following negation attaches to an omitted predicate, and that اليوم here is governed by عليكم, though the reverse analysis is also possible.
rows.anchor: وذكر الرضي أن الظرف بعد النفي لايتعلق بالمنفي بل بمحذوف وهو خبر وأن ( اليوم ) في الآية معمول ( عليكم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing makes the omitted predicate ذاك and attaches اليوم to يغفر الله لكم.
rows.anchor: جوز أيضا كون الخبر ذاك و ( اليوم ) متعلقا بقوله : ( ( يغفر الله لكم

rows.speaker: المرتضى
rows.claim: Some weaken al-Murtada's attachment of اليوم to the forgiveness clause on the ground that a prayer cannot govern what precedes it.
rows.anchor: ونقل عن المرتضى أنه قال في الدرر : قد ضعف هذا قوم من جهة أن الدعاء لاينصب ماقبله

rows.speaker: ابن المنير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Munir argues that reading Joseph's words as certain news of forgiveness conflicts with the brothers' later request that Jacob seek forgiveness for them.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن المنير : لو كان متعلقا به لقطعوا بالمغفرة باخبار الصديق ولم يكن كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi finds that objection unpersuasive: forgiveness in the sense of concealment from punishment occurs on Judgment Day, and knowing through a truthful report that forgiveness will occur does not make asking for it pointless.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأنه لاطائل تحته لأن المغفرة وهي ستر الذنب يوم القيامة حتى لايؤاخذوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers may have asked Jacob to forgive offenses against his own rights, and may not yet have believed Joseph was a prophet.
rows.anchor: وقد يقال أيضا : إن الذي طلبوه من أبيهم مغفرة ما يتعلق به ويرجع إلى حقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi favors taking the clause as a supplication: most readers pause after اليوم, and al-Tabari and Ibn Ishaq also prefer a prayer rather than a declaration of certain forgiveness.
rows.anchor: أكثر القراء على الوقف على ( اليوم ) وهو ظاهر في عدم تعلقه بيغفر وهو اختيار الطبري وابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who read the words as a declaration say Joseph's forgiveness of the brothers entails that God will forgive them too, in keeping with God's promise to accept repentance.
rows.anchor: ذهب جمع أيضا إلى كونه خبرا والحكم بذلك مع أنه غيب قيل : لأنه عليه السلام صفح عن جريمتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All mercy shown by creatures comes from God; even when it benefits another, it also relieves the merciful person of spiritual distress. God alone forgives every scale of sin and accepts the penitent.
rows.anchor: فان كل من يرحم سواه جل وعلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Joseph's brothers were embarrassed to eat with him because of their past, and he replied that his standing in Egyptians' eyes was greater now that they knew he was Abraham's descendant and his brothers were present.
rows.anchor: ومن كرم يوسف عليه السلام ما روى أن أخوته أرسلوا اليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the king wanted Joseph involved in everything except the king's household; Joseph answered that he had greater grounds for pride as the son of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
rows.anchor: وكذا ماأخرجه سعيد بن منصور وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shirt is apparently the one Joseph wore at the time; another report from Ibn Abbas and others identifies it as Abraham's shirt from Paradise, kept in a silver tube and worn by Joseph as an amulet that healed illness by God's permission. Alusi says the objection from Jacob smelling it is weak.
rows.anchor: هو القميص الذي كان عليه حينئذ كما هو الظاهر وعن ابن عباس وغيره أنه القميص الذي كساه الله تعالى إبراهيم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A further view identifies the shirt as the one torn from the back to show that Joseph had been protected from sexual wrongdoing; Alusi calls this remote.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو القميص الذي قد من دبر وأرسله ليعلم أنه عصم من الفاحشة ولا يخفى بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in بقميصي can mark accompaniment or state, or be causative, meaning to send the shirt itself.
rows.anchor: فالباء اما للمصاحبة أو للملابسة أي أذهبوا مصحوبين أو ملتبسين به أو للتعدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يأت بصيرا can mean that Jacob becomes seeing or that he comes to Joseph with his sight restored; the second reading better explains why Joseph orders the shirt's placement, since the desired result is his arrival sighted.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن صيرورته بصيرا أمر مفروغ عنه مقطوع إنما الكلام في تسبب الإلقاء لاتيانه كذلك فهذا الوجه أرجح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أهلكم covers women, children, and everyone included by the word family. Joseph does not order his brothers to bring their father as though he were subject to them, but assumes Jacob will choose to come.
rows.anchor: من النساء والذراري وغيرهم مما ينتظمه لفظ الأهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph knew Jacob was blind either because the brothers told him or through revelation; he knew the shirt's effect through revelation or prior experience if it was the amulet shirt, while revelation is necessary on the more apparent identification.
rows.anchor: علم يوسف عليه السلام بذلك يحتمل أن يكون باعلامهم ويحتمل أن يكون بالوحي

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam offers a rational medical account: Jacob's grief and crying weakened his sight, while joy at Joseph's shirt strengthened his heart and vital spirit and restored vision; Alusi says he does not accept this explanation.
rows.anchor: وقال الامام : يمكن أن يقال : لعل يوسف عليه السلام علم أن أباه ما عرا بصره ما عراه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi estimates the family Joseph summoned at about seventy people.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي : وكان أولئك الأهل نحوا من سبعين انسانا

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ b. Anas reports from Ibn Abi Hatim that Jacob's descendants numbered seventy-two.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن الربيع بن أنس أنهم اثنان وسبعون من ولده وولد ولده

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud is reported by Ibn al-Mundhir and others to give a count of ninety-three; other estimates in the passage are eighty, ninety, and ninety-six.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر وغيره عن ابن مسعود أنهم ثلاثة وتسعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Jacob's family grew in Egypt and left with Moses as 600,570 men, besides children and elderly people; another reported count gives 1,200,000 descendants.
rows.anchor: فخرجوا منها مع موسى عليه السلام وهم ستمائة ألف وخمسمائة وبضعة وسبعون رجلا سوى الذرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers mean Jacob has long been wrong about Joseph, through excessive love, constant mention, and expectation of reunion; the phrasing suggests this fixation has persisted.
rows.anchor: أي لفي ذهابك عن الصواب قدما بالافراط في محبة يوسف والاكثار من ذكره والتوقع للقائه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets ضلال as love.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن مجاهد أن الضلال هنا بمعنى الحب

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil interprets ضلال as misery and hardship.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : هو الشقاء والعناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations take ضلال to mean destruction or disappearance, by analogy with saying that water disappeared into milk; Saʿid b. Jubayr reports madness, which Alusi says is unsuitable.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الهلاك والذهاب من قولهم : ضل الماء في اللبن أي ذهب فيه وهلك وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada calls the brothers' statement harsh and says people like them should not have said it to someone like Jacob; Alusi suggests they said it because they thought Joseph was dead.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : لقد قالوا كلمة غليظة لاينبغي أن يقولها مثلهم لمثله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the bearer of good news as Judah; a report says Judah volunteered because he had brought Jacob the shirt of grief and wanted to bring the shirt of joy.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد هو يهوذا روى أنه قال لأخوته قد علمتم أني ذهبت إلى أبي بقميص الترحة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One narration from Ibn Abbas identifies the messenger as Malik b. Dhʿar, though the passage says Ibn Abbas's better-known report gives another identification.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية عن ابن عباس أنه مالك بن ذعر والرواية الشهيرة عنه ما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle أن after لما is redundant and regularly occurs there; Ibn Masʿud's interpretive reading says the messenger came ahead of the caravan.
rows.anchor: و ( أن ) صلة وقد أطردت زيادتها بعد لما وقرأ ابن مسعود وعد ذلك قراءة تفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of ألقى may be the messenger, which fits Joseph's instruction and weighs against identifying him as Malik, or Jacob himself; the latter is said to suit propriety, and Farqad reports that Jacob smelled the shirt and placed it on his eyes.
rows.anchor: وقيل : فاعل ( ألقى ) ضمير يعقوب عليه السلام أيضا والأول أوفق بقوله : ( فألقوه ) على وجه أبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The face likely means the whole face, as people wipe their faces with something believed blessed; it can also stand for the eyes or for the whole in place of a part.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه اريد بالوجه كله وقد جرت العادة أنه متى وجد الانسان شيئا يعتقد فيه البركة مسح به وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians take ارتد as a sister of كان meaning became, with بصيرا its predicate; Abu Hayyan instead treats بصيرا as a circumstantial accusative and says Jacob returned to his former sighted state.
rows.anchor: عند بعضهم من أخوات كان وهي بمعنى صار فبصيرا خبرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi rejects the claim that بصيرا is intensive because it is an active participle from بصر, and even an adjective on the فعيل pattern meaning an agent or patient is not necessarily emphatic.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأن فعيلا هنا ليس للمبالغة أذ ما يكون لها هو المعدول عن فاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's restored sight through the shirt is apparently a breach of ordinary nature; a proposed explanation is that joy revived his heart and bodily heat, but the passage also compares it with lovers being healed by the breeze from a beloved's land.
rows.anchor: وأياما كان الظاهر أن عوده عليه السلام بصيرا بالقاء القميص على وجهه ليس الا من باب خرق العادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet says a breeze from the beloved's land heals the speaker, illustrating the claim about lovers finding cure in the scent of their beloved's country.
rows.anchor: بكل غمامة يهب بها من نحو أرضك ريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another unnamed poet addresses the morning breeze as a healer carrying Salma's scent after hearing of the speaker's illness.
rows.anchor: كلما تقربت منا فاح نشرك طيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Jacob asked how Joseph was; when told he was king of Egypt, Jacob asked about his religion, and on hearing he remained Muslim declared that the blessing was now complete.
rows.anchor: وجاء في بعض الاخبار أنه عليه السلام سأل البشير كيف يوسف قال : ملك مصر فقال : ما أصنع بالملك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Abu al-Shaykh transmits from al-Hasan that the messenger found Jacob's household without food or bread for seven days, then prayed that God ease Jacob's death throes.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أبو الشيخ عن الحسن قال : لما جاء البشير اليه عليه السلام قال : ما وجدت عندنا شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report has Jacob say he does not know how to reward the messenger, then make a prayer for him.
rows.anchor: وجاء في رواية أنه قال له : ماأدري ما أثيبك اليوم ثم دعا له بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ألم أقل لكم may address those previously with Jacob, recalling his statement that he smelled Joseph, or the arriving sons; the latter fits the following words better and recalls his order to search and not despair of God's mercy.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون خطابا لمن كان عنده من قبل أي ألم أقل لكم أني لأجد ريح يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi favors the arriving sons as the addressees, with the statement recalling his instruction when sending them to search and avoid despair; the following clause is what God had taught him about Joseph's survival.
rows.anchor: واستظهر في البحر كونها مقول القول وهو كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers invoke Jacob's fatherhood to stir affection and compassion; their admission of sin presents forgiveness and intercession as fitting for someone who confesses wrongdoing, and their confidence in his pardon explains why they simply ask him to seek forgiveness.
rows.anchor: ونادوه بعنوان الابوة تحريكا للعطف والشفقة وعللوا ذلك بقولهم : ( ( انا كنا خاطئين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another explanation is that by calling him father they appeal to his compassion: without his intercession they would be lost, but Alusi says this reading is unconvincing.
rows.anchor: وقيل : حيث نادوه بذلك أرادوا ومن حق شفقتك علينا أن تستغفر لنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet through Ibn Abbas says Jacob postponed the prayer until the predawn period, when supplication is answered.
rows.anchor: روى عن ابن عباس مرفوعا أنه عليه السلام أخر الاستغفار لهم إلى السحر لأن الدعاء فيه مستجاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report attributed to Ibn Abbas says Jacob delayed the prayer until Friday night; it appears in a long hadith that al-Tirmidhi graded good.
rows.anchor: وروى عنه أيضا كذلك أنه أخره إلى ليلة الجمعة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Jacob put off the prayer until night worship; Ibn Jubayr and a group say he waited for the white nights, when prayer is answered.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير وفرقة : إلى الليالي البيض

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says Jacob waited to ask Joseph whether he had pardoned his brothers before praying for them.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي : أخره حتى يسأل يوسف عليه السلام فان عفا عنهم استغفر لهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view says Jacob waited to test whether their repentance was sincere; some object that سوف indicates a longer delay than these short intervals, while Alusi cites grammarians who equate it with سين and says any postponement, even an hour, fits.
rows.anchor: وقيل أخر ليعلم حالهم في صدق التوبة وتعقب بعضهم بعض هذه الأقوال بأن سوف تأبى ذلك

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A further view takes سوف as promising continued prayer for the brothers; this depends on the disputed claim that both future particles mark continuity, though some reports indicate he prayed for them over a period.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أراد عليه السلام الدوام على الاستغفار لهم وهو مبني على أن السين وسوف يدلان على الاستمرار

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits from Anas a report that the sons, fearing God's judgment despite Jacob and Joseph's pardon, asked both to pray; Gabriel later told Jacob that God had accepted the prayer and forgiven them, after a delay of twenty years.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير عن أنس بن مالك قال إن الله تعالى لما جمع شمله ببنيه وأقر عينه خلا ولده نجيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says the Anas account is unsound; if true, its claim that the brothers were promised prophethood afterward would imply they were prophets and that their sins preceded prophethood.
rows.anchor: قيل : وهذا إن صح دليل على نبوتهم وإن ما صدر منهم كان قبل استنبائهم والحق عدم الصحة

rows.speaker: ابن عائشة
rows.claim: Abu al-Shaykh transmits from Ibn ʿAʾisha that the sons were not forgiven even after twenty years until Gabriel taught Jacob a prayer to seek mercy, aid, and repentance for the believers; Jacob recited it at predawn and they were forgiven.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أبو الشيخ عن ابن عائشة قال : ماتيب على ولد يعقوب إلا بعد عشرين سنة

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj, through Abu ʿUbayd and others, suggests the Qur'anic order is rearranged and that Jacob's words should include إن شاء الله; Alusi says this claim should be disregarded because the words are unquestionably Jacob's and he sees no reason for the rearrangement.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أبو عبيد وغيره عن ابن جريج ان ما سيأتي إن شاء الله متعلق بهذا وهو من تقديم القرآن وتأخيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istaghfara can take two objects, as Ibn Hisham notes. In the brothers' request the first object, God, is omitted and their sins named; in Jacob's reply the Lord is named and the sins omitted.
rows.anchor: الصحيح أن ( استغفر ) متعد إلى مفعولين يقال : إستغفرت الله الذنب وقد نص على ذلك ابن هشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omitting God in the brothers' request broadens the plea to include everyone they wronged, while naming their sins explicitly records their confession; naming the Lord in Jacob's reply focuses on seeking God's favor, which brings others' favor, and the omitted sins are clear from the recent context.
rows.anchor: ولعل السر والله سبحانه أعلم أن حذف الأول من الأول لإرادة التعميم أي استغفر لنا كل من أذنبنا في حقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of delayed prayer may deepen the brothers' reliance on God and make the desired forgiveness more likely.
rows.anchor: ولعل التسويف على هذا ليزداد انقطاعهم إلى الله تعالى فيكون ذلك أرجى لحصول المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Joseph sent two hundred camels to bring his father and household; the Torah says he gave each brother a robe, Benjamin three hundred dirhams and five robes, and Jacob ten donkeys loaded with gifts plus ten loaded with grain and food.
rows.anchor: روى أنه عليه السلام جهز إلى أبيه جهازا ومائتي راحلة ليتجهز اليه بمن معه وفي التوراة أنه عليه السلام أعطى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Joseph and the king went out with four thousand soldiers and dignitaries and all Egypt to receive Jacob; Judah supported the old man as they walked, and Jacob mistook the king for Pharaoh before Judah told him it was Joseph.
rows.anchor: في أربعة آلاف من الجند والعظماء وأهل مصر بأجمعهم لاستقباله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the report, Joseph was prevented from greeting his father first so Jacob's greater standing with God would be evident; Jacob embraced Joseph and greeted him as the one who had taken his sorrows away.
rows.anchor: فلما لقيه ذهب يوسف عليه السلام ليبدأه بالسلام فمنع ذلك ليعلم أن يعقوب أكرم على الله تعالى منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob says his grief and crying blinded him even though the resurrection reunites them; another account says he feared Joseph might lose his religion and be separated from him in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وجاء أنه عليه السلام قال لأبيه : ياأبت بكيت علي حتى ذهب بصرك ألم تعلم أن القيامة تجمعنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative compresses Jacob's journey: he traveled with his household until they reached Joseph, and the meeting is reported to have occurred on Ashura.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام إيجاز والتقدير فرحل يعقوب عليه السلام بأهله وساروا حتى أتوا يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آوى إليهما means that Joseph drew his parents to himself and embraced them; the parents are identified as Jacob and his maternal aunt Leah, or Rachel, with the aunt treated as a mother because of her compassion and role as stepmother.
rows.anchor: أي ضمهما اليه واعتنقهما والمراد بهما أبوه وخالته ليا وقيل : راحيل وليس بذاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas explains that Leah, Jacob's wife after Joseph's mother died, counted as a mother because the stepmother is called a mother and takes her place.
rows.anchor: وروى هذا عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

rows.speaker: الزهراوي
rows.claim: Al-Zahrawi reports another view that the parents were Jacob and Joseph's maternal grandmother.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : المراد أبوه وجدته أم أمه حكاه الزهراوي

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن اسحاق
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn Ishaq say Joseph's mother was still alive; although the passage also reports that she died after Benjamin's birth, they say God revived her so the dream would come true. Alusi says this is unestablished and would have become famous.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن وابن اسحاق : إن أمه عليه السلام كانت بالحياة فلا حاجة إلى التأويل

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: The codex of ʿAbd Allah reads the phrase as Joseph drawing in his parents and brothers.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف عبدالله ( آوى اليه أبويه واخوته )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The family may have first met Joseph at a camp outside town, after which he invited them into Egypt, giving two distinct entries; alternatively they met him in Egypt and the command means to settle there.
rows.anchor: فدخلوا عليه فيه فآواهما اليه ثم طلب منهم الدخول في البلدة فهناك دخولان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are promised safety from famine and other hardships. The exception is attached to the promise of safety, not the command to enter, since the condition belongs with a promise rather than an order.
rows.anchor: أي من القحط وسائر المكاره والاستثناء مافي التيسير داخل في الأمن لافي الأمر بالدخول

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari makes the condition govern entering in a state of safety: the omitted consequent is that, if God wills, they will enter safely, and the condition interrupts between the circumstantial phrase and its subject.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشاف أن المشيئة تعلقت بالدخول المكيف بالأمن لأن القصد إلى اتصافهم بالأمن في دخولهم

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi reads the wording as having the force of a prayer; Al-Kashf says the manner of entry is part of the command but denies that it is a prayer. Alusi sides with al-Tibi.
rows.anchor: وإلى ذلك ذهب العلامة الطيبي وقال في الكشف : ان فيه اشارة إلى أن الكيفية مقصودة بالامر

rows.speaker: صاحب الفرائد
rows.claim: The author of al-Fara'id supplies an omitted clause meaning, 'if God wills, you will enter safely,' making آمنين modify the omitted consequent and avoiding interruption or reordered syntax; Alusi objects that the conditional parenthesis functions like an opening invocation for blessing and reads naturally as an aside.
rows.anchor: وزعم صاحب الفرائد أن التقدير ادخلوا مصر إن شاء الله دخلتم آمنين فآمنين متعلق بالجزاء المحذوف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others take the throne as a couch or bed; Joseph raised his parents onto it in special honor beyond what he did for his brothers.
rows.anchor: على السير كما قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وغيرهما تكرما لهما فوق ما فعله بالاخوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in they fell in prostration includes both parents and brothers; taking it to mean only the brothers does not fit the dream that all of them prostrated.
rows.anchor: أي أبواه واخوته وقيل : الضمير للاخوة فقط وليس بذاك فان الرؤيا تقتضي أن يكون الابوان والاخوة خروا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense is that they fell with their foreheads down in prostration, expressed as a prospective circumstantial state because the prostration followed the fall; such prostration was then a customary form of greeting and honor.
rows.anchor: أي على الجباه كما هو الظاهر وهو كما قال أبو البقاء حال مقدرة لأن السجود يكون بعد الخرور

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says prostration was the greeting of kings; God gave this community salutation, the greeting of the people of Paradise, as an honor in advance.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : كان السجود تحية الملوك عندهم وأعطى الله تعالى هذه الامة السلام تحية أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations reduce the prostration to a nod, a deep bow without placing the forehead down, or humility; another reads خروا as passing over, as in the cited verse, though Alusi says falling is the apparent meaning.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ما كان ذلك الا ايماء بالرأس وقيل : كان كالركوع البالغ دون وضع الجبهة على الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A view attributed to Ibn Abbas says they prostrated to God, not Joseph, in gratitude for the blessing; Alusi says the lām in both places and the dream's wording weigh against it, though another says the lām means 'because of' or 'toward'.
rows.anchor: ونسب لابن عباس أن المعنى خروا لأجل يوسف سجدا لله شكرا على ماأوزعهم من النعمة

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam favors prostration to God because the wording places the throne first, whereas prostration to Joseph would seem more humble before his elevation; he also argues Joseph's religion and character would not allow him to accept his father prostrating.
rows.anchor: وذكر الامام أن القول بأن السجود كان لله تعالى لا ليوسف عليه السلام حسن والدليل عليه أن قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Imam's argument from sequence is not decisive because narrated order need not be event order; another answer is that God commanded Jacob, as prophetic dreams can impose a duty, or that Jacob complied with a divine test.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأن تأخير الخرور عن الرفع ليس بنص في المقصود لأن الترتيب الذكري لايجب كونه على وفق الترتيب الوقوعي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report says Jacob was startled and shuddered when he saw his parents and brothers prostrate to Joseph.
rows.anchor: لما رأى سجود أبويه واخوته له هاله ذلك واقشعر جلده منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The act may have been a divine trial, or a way to make the brothers follow their father so old grudges would not reignite and Joseph would not be prevented from forgiving them.
rows.anchor: ولا يبعد أن يكون ذلك من تمام تشديد الله تعالى على يعقوب عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some restrict the prostration to the brothers to avoid attributing it to Jacob, but the dream requires both parents and brothers; the Imam replies that a dream need not be fulfilled in every visual detail, since the family's migration itself honored Joseph.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من ذهب إلى أن ذلك السجود لم يكن الا من الاخوة فرارا من نسبته إلى يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi concludes that both parents and brothers prostrated; he leans toward a bow like the greeting used by non-Arabs, which could still involve falling down.
rows.anchor: والحق أن السجود بأي معنى كان وقع من الأبوين والاخوة جميعا والقلب يميل ألى أنه كان انحناء كتحية الاعاجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من قبل means before the brothers' prostration or before these events; it can modify the dream, its interpretation, or be an omitted circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: أي من قبل سجودكم أو من قبل هذه الحوادث والظرف متعلق برؤياي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حقا means truly: the dream may be called true figuratively, or the word may be the second object of جعل بمعنى صير, a circumstantial phrase, an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, or a semantically related verbal noun.
rows.anchor: أي صدقا والرؤيا توصف بذلك ولو مجازا وأعربه جمع على أنه مفعول ثان لجعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in أحسن بي is unusual because احسن normally governs إلى or ل; it can be explained by comparison with Qur'anic usage or by treating أحسن as carrying the sense of لطف. Alusi says usage and al-Asas attest باء for لطف.
rows.anchor: الأصل كما في البحر أن يتعدى الاحسان بإلى أو اللام كقوله تعالى : ( وأحسن كما أحسن الله اليك )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about leaving prison may attach to أحسن or an implicit verbal noun; if إذ is causal, the favor is Joseph's release from prison and associated deliverance, while a temporal reading points to other favors.
rows.anchor: منصوب بأحسن أو بالمصدر المحذوف عند من يرى جواز ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph mentions prison rather than the pit to avoid reminding his brothers of their offense; the brothers are apparently present, and the favor was completed after prison when Joseph reached the king, escaped slavery, and cleared his name.
rows.anchor: ولم يصرح عليه السلام بقصة الجب حذرا من تثريب اخوته وتناسيا لما جرى منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: البدو is the open countryside, named because its features are visible, then came to mean wilderness generally; Jacob's household lived in the Syrian borderlands with camels and sheep. Al-Zamakhshari describes them as tent-dwelling herders who moved between water and pasture.
rows.anchor: البسيط من الأرض وانما سمي بذلك لأن مافيه يبدو للناظر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Jacob moved to the countryside only after becoming a prophet because God never sent a prophet from the countryside; Ibn Abbas says Jacob settled in Badā and had a mosque beneath its mountain.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن يعقوب عليه السلام انما تحول إلى البادية بعد النبوة لأن الله تعالى لم يبعث نبيا من البادية

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says Badā is a named location between Shuʿb and Badā, cited in a poem by Jamil; on this reading the family came from visiting that place and were settled people, an explanation al-Alusi calls far from the apparent sense.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الانباري : إن بدا اسم موضع معروف يقال : هو بين شعب وبدا وهما موضعان ذكرهما جميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb نزغ describes Satan's provocation and corruption, originally a prod to a kneeling animal that makes it run; Satan is the agent figuratively through whispering. Joseph's wording avoids reproaching his brothers and highlights the grace of relief after hardship.
rows.anchor: أي أفسد وحرش وأصله من نزع الرابض الدابة اذا نخسها

rows.speaker: الجبائي والكعبي والقاضي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i, al-Kaʿbi, and the Qadi use the verse to argue against predestination; Alusi says the inference is questionable.
rows.anchor: واستدل الجبائي والكعبي والقاضي بالآية على بطلان الجبر وفيه نظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لطيف لما يشاء means that God subtly manages what He wills: no difficult matter can resist His will, and He makes its causes easy. The lām attaches to لطيف on this reading; an alternative takes it causally as 'for what He wills'.
rows.anchor: أي لطيف التدبير له اذ ما من صعب الا وتنفذ فيه مشيئته تعالى ويتسهل دونها

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says لطيف is the opposite of dense and describes light movement or delicate affairs; as an attribute of God it signifies knowledge of fine details and gentleness toward servants.
rows.anchor: والى هذا يشير كلام الراغب حيث قال : اللطيف ضد الكثيف ويعبر باللطيف عن الحركة الخفيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Wise is the one who does everything according to wisdom.
rows.anchor: الذي يفعل كل شيء على وجه الحكمة لاغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Joseph showed Jacob his storehouses; at the paper archive Jacob asked why Joseph had not written during the eight stages between them. Joseph said Gabriel instructed him not to; Gabriel said God commanded this because Jacob had once said he feared the wolf would eat Joseph. Jacob then asked whether Joseph had not feared him.
rows.anchor: يوسف طاف بأبيه عليهما السلام في خزائنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say revelation instructed Joseph to keep his survival hidden from his father until the appointed time, giving a clear excuse for not sending word.
rows.anchor: وقد صرح غير واحد بأنه عليه السلام أوحى اليه باخفاء الامر على أبيه إلى أن يبلغ الكتاب أجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi raises why Jacob, a widely known prophet grieving his beloved son for so long, never heard the news even though Joseph was nearby, prominent, and publicly called people to God; the answer is that this concealment was a breach of ordinary nature.
rows.anchor: لكن يبقى السؤال بأن يعقوب عليه السلام كان من أكابر الانبياء نفسا وأبا وجدا وكان مشهورا في أكناف الأرض

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reports a period of eighty years between the dream and its fulfillment.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عبدالله بن أحمد في زاوئد الزهد عن الحسن أن المدة ثمانون سنة

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports through Ibn Jarir that the interval was ninety-seven years; other reports give eighteen, seventy, thirty-five, or forty years, with forty attributed to Salman and called the majority view.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن جريج أنها سبع وتسعون سنة وعن حذيفة أنها سبعون سنة

rows.speaker: ابن شداد
rows.claim: Ibn Shaddad says the time needed for a dream to reach its interpretation ends at forty years.
rows.anchor: قال ابن شداد : والى ذلك ينتهي تأويل الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من الملك means a substantial portion of kingship, with من partitive; readings that make it extra or explanatory are unlikely. Some supply 'great' as an object, which Alusi rejects. The kingdom may mean Egypt specifically or broader dominion, but Joseph was not fully independent.
rows.anchor: فمن للتبعيض ويبعد القول بزيادتها أو جعلها لبيان الجنس والتعظيم من مقتضيات المقام

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Other interpretations make the kingdom mastery over oneself and one's desires, or, in Ataa's view, control of one's rivals through obedience and attainment of wishes; Alusi says Ataa's explanation is weak.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء : ملك حساده بالطاعة ونيل الاماني وليس بذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أحاديث here means some of the interpretation of events, apparently dream interpretation; alternatively it means understanding hidden meanings of revealed books and the prophets' practices. Joseph was not taught all of it.
rows.anchor: والمراد بتأويل الأحاديث أما تعليم تعبير الرؤيا وهو الظاهر واما تفهيم غوامض أسرار الكتب الالهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order is less apparent if the phrase means dream interpretation; perhaps kingdom is listed first because it is more evidently a gift from God, though teaching is also a great gift.
rows.anchor: فلعل تقديم ايتاء الملك على ذلك في الذكر

rows.speaker: عبد الله وابن ذر
rows.claim: Abd Allah and Ibn Dharr read آتيتني and علمتني without the final yāʾ, relying on the preceding kasra; Ibn Atiyya also transmits from Ibn Dharr a reading without قد.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبدالله وابن ذر ( آتيتن وعلمتن ) بحذف الياء فيهما اكتفاء بالكسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فاطر means originator and creator; it can parse as an adjective of رب, an appositive or explanatory phrase, an implied 'I mean', or a second vocative. The renewed description as Creator emphasizes the grounds for the following request.
rows.anchor: أي مبدعهما وخالقهما ونصبه على أنه نعت لرب أو بدل أو بيان أو منصوب بأعنى أو منادى ثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولي means one who manages, guarantees, supports, or befriends Joseph; it may also mean مولى, the giver of blessings in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: متولى أموري ومتكفل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: توفني means take me in death.
rows.anchor: توفني ( أقبضني ( مسلما والحقني بالصالحين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the righteous Joseph asks to join are his forefathers; another view takes them as all righteous people in rank and honor.
rows.anchor: من آبائي على ما روى عن ابن عباس أو بعامة الصالحين في الرتبة والكرامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that Joseph was already a great prophet asking to join people at the lowest level is answered by humility, as in prophets' seeking forgiveness; it does not arise if he means his noble forefathers. Righteousness itself has degrees, and he means an honored rank.
rows.anchor: والحق أن يقال : إن الصلاح مقول بالتشكيك متفاوت قوة وضعفا والمقام يقتضي أنه عليه السلام أراد بالصالحين

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam offers a mystical account: souls that share divine illumination reflect light to one another like polished mirrors, increasing its brightness until weak eyes cannot bear it; Alusi regards the account as it appears, without adopting it.
rows.anchor: وقال الامام : ههنا وههنا مقام آخر في الآية على لسان اصحاب المكاشفات وهو أن النفوس المفارقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many commentators take Joseph's words as a wish for death; the Imam says a rational person may desire death after recognizing human imperfection, the transience and mixed character of worldly pleasure, and the relief it brings from bodily appetite and anxiety.
rows.anchor: أن المفسرين اختلفوا في أن هذا هل هو منه عليه السلام تمنى للموت وطلب منه أم لا فالكثير منهم على أنه طلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say that wishing for death out of love for meeting God is permitted; the two canonical collections report from Aisha that whoever loves to meet God is loved by God in return.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر غير واحد أن تمني الموت حبا للقاء الله تعالى مما لابأس به وقد روى الشيخان عن عائشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wishing for death because of a calamity is forbidden, according to the report that none should wish for death on account of hardship.
rows.anchor: نعم تمنى الموت عند نزول البلاء منهي عنه ففي الخبر لايتمنين أحدكم الموت لضر نزل به

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another group says Joseph did not wish for death; he prayed for Islam to continue through the rest of his life, then for death when his appointed time came.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم : انه عليه السلام لم يتمن الموت وانما عدد نعم الله تعالى عليه ثم دعا بأن تدوم تلك النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both readings can be reconciled: the prophets' eventual death in Islam is assured, but Islam here can mean submission to whatever God decrees, or the wording stresses that even an assured outcome depends on God's will.
rows.anchor: والحاصل أنه عليه السلام انما طلب الموافاة على الاسلام لا الوفاة ولا يرد على القولين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Those who think Joseph requested death say he died within a week; al-Hasan instead says he lived many more years after the prayer.
rows.anchor: والذاهبون إلى الاول قالوا أنه عليه السلام لم يأت عليه أسبوع حتى توفاه الله تعالى وكان الحسن يذهب إلى القول الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Historical reports say Jacob lived with Joseph twenty-four years, then died and was buried in Syria by his father's grave; Joseph lived another twenty-three years or more, eventually asked for death, and died at 120 or 107. Egyptians fought over his burial, so he was placed in a marble casket in the Nile until Moses removed it roughly four hundred years later for burial with the ancestors.
rows.anchor: وروى المؤرخون ان يعقوب عليه السلام أقام مع يوسف أربعا وعشرين سنة ثم توفى وأوصى أن يدفن بالشام

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah says Jacob lived seventeen years after arriving in Egypt at age 130 and later asked to be buried with his ancestors; Joseph lived to age 110 and asked his brothers to carry his bones back when God returned them to the promised land, and was embalmed in a coffin until Moses carried it out.
rows.anchor: وفي التوراة أن يوسف عليه السلام أسكن أباه وإخوته في مكان يقال له عين شمس من أرض السدير وبقي هناك سبع عشرة سنة
